record.paper: On an induced version of Menger's theorem

dossier_meta.paper: On an induced version of Menger's theorem
dossier_meta.statement_text: For every $d, \Delta \in \mathbb{N}$ there exists a constant $C = C(d, \Delta) > 0$ such that the following holds. If $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $G$ is a graph with $\Delta(G) \leq \Delta$ and $X, Y \subseteq V(G)$, then there exists either (1) $k$ $X$-$Y$-paths pairwise at distance at least $d$ in $G$, or (2) a set of less than $Ck$ vertices in $G$ which separates $X$ and $Y$.
dossier_meta.context_text: This conjecture is derived as a consequence of the stronger (c independent of k) form of Conjecture 1.2 for graphs of bounded maximum degree $\Delta$: the ball $B_G(Z, cd)$ can be bounded in size by $\Delta^{cd+1}k$, yielding a linear separator of size $Ck$. The paper proves this conjecture in the first non-trivial case $d = 2$ as its first main result (Theorem 1.5).
